rubrics.rubric: Are the three required deliverables present and named exactly as instructed?
criterion: The updated gradebook is delivered as SOC101_Fall2024_Gradebook.xlsx.
The dispute decisions are delivered as grade_dispute_decisions.csv.
The assessment report is delivered as SOC101_Fall2024_Assessment_Report.docx.

rubrics.rubric: Does the updated gradebook correctly normalize and calculate Final_Grade and Letter_Grade for all 35 students?
criterion: The Assignments sheet contains a Final_Grade column.
The Assignments sheet contains a Letter_Grade column.
All 35 students have a Final_Grade.
Component maximum scores are derived from the gradebook data.
Each component is normalized to a percentage before weighting.
The seven instructed weights are applied.
Blank component scores count as zero.
Final_Grade is reported on a 0–100 scale.
Letter_Grade uses only A, B, C, D, or F.
Letter boundaries are applied to the unrounded percentage.
The calculated values agree with the source assignment scores.

rubrics.rubric: Do the grade-dispute decisions adjudicate both named appeals from the available records without imposing an unsupported outcome?
criterion: The CSV uses exactly the eight required columns.
The CSV contains one row for SOC24008.
The CSV contains one row for SOC24023.
Each Current_Letter_Grade agrees with the unadjusted gradebook calculation.
The SOC24008 decision considers both missing high-weight components.
The SOC24008 justification uses comparable academic performance and documented office-hours engagement.
The SOC24008 decision explains why an Incomplete, estimated scores, or no adjustment is supported by the available evidence.
The SOC24023 decision does not apply an attendance penalty absent from the published weights.
The SOC24023 justification checks the claimed proximity to a grade boundary against the calculated percentage.
Adjusted_Grade clearly states the resulting grade or temporary status.

rubrics.rubric: Does the assessment report present source-correct grade distributions by section and overall?
criterion: Section A reports its student count.
Section B reports its student count.
Overall reports the total student count.
Counts are reported for A, B, C, D, and F in each group.
Percentages are reported for A, B, C, D, and F in each group.
Counts reconcile to each group's N.
Percentages are calculated from the displayed counts.
The distributions agree with the updated gradebook.

rubrics.rubric: Does the assignment-level section report the required normalized statistics and accurately identify the largest inter-section gaps?
criterion: Exam1 mean, median, and standard deviation are reported by section.
Exam2 mean, median, and standard deviation are reported by section.
Midterm_Essay mean, median, and standard deviation are reported by section.
Final_Essay mean, median, and standard deviation are reported by section.
Quiz_Avg mean, median, and standard deviation are reported by section.
Discussion_Posts mean, median, and standard deviation are reported by section.
Research_Proposal mean, median, and standard deviation are reported by section.
All descriptive statistics use normalized percentages.
Population or sample standard deviation is accepted when the same convention is applied consistently to every component and section.
The largest mean gap is identified from the submitted calculations.
Relevant differences in central tendency are discussed.
Relevant differences in spread are discussed without requiring named example students.

rubrics.rubric: Does the course-evaluation benchmarking section correctly compare all ten SOC 101 items with the OpenIntro evals baseline?
criterion: The institutional baseline is calculated from the evals.csv score column.
The baseline calculation uses the available non-missing records.
Each of the ten Course_Eval_Summary items is compared with the baseline.
A numeric difference is reported for each item.
Items above the baseline are identified.
Items below the baseline are identified.
The analysis acknowledges that the external overall-score dataset is not a perfectly matched item-level comparator.
The reported values agree with the two named input files.

rubrics.rubric: Does the At-Risk Student Summary identify every student meeting the instructed rule and provide complete support information?
criterion: Every student with an F-range Final_Grade is included.
Every student with four or more absences is included.
Every student with two or more missing assignments is included.
Each listed student has Final_Grade.
Each listed student has an absence count.
Late marks are reported.
Missing assignments are identified.
Office-hours visit count is reported.
Office-hours dates are reported.
Office-hours topics are reported.
Each student has a source-responsive recommended intervention.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Essay Assessment Quality Review use every provided rubric category and propose a specific evidence-based Spring 2025 modification?
criterion: Thesis is referenced by name.
Argumentation is referenced by name.
Originality is referenced by name.
Organization and Writing is referenced by name.
Use of Evidence is referenced by name.
Application of Readings or Concepts is referenced by name.
Midterm_Essay score distributions are discussed.
Final_Essay score distributions are discussed.
The report does not infer category-level performance from aggregate essay scores without qualification.
The Spring 2025 modification is specific.
The Spring 2025 modification is actionable.
The modification responds to the observed assessment evidence.

rubrics.rubric: Does the assessment report meet the required audience, section order, reflection, and presentation requirements?
criterion: The report is addressed to Dr. Patricia Hernandez as Department Chair.
The report is signed by Dr. Michael Torres as Assistant Professor of Sociology.
The six required headed sections appear in the instructed order.
The Reflection contains two or three substantive paragraphs.
The Reflection identifies what went well using specific evidence.
The Reflection identifies what needs improvement using specific evidence.
The Reflection proposes one concrete data-informed pedagogical change.
The report has a clear title or header identifying the SOC 101 Fall 2024 assessment.
The required grade-distribution table and any other tables used have readable row and column labels and values.
